message: "orders"."ref" is converted to varchar(8) with substring() in USING, which can keep only part of each value. Whatever it drops is lost.
why: A USING expression replaces every value with its result. Functions such as left(), substring(), and round(), and an explicit cast to varchar(n), drop part of a value without any error, and the original cannot be recovered. Without USING, PostgreSQL fails on a value that does not fit instead of cutting it.
safeAlternative: Check first that no value would be cut, for example with a SELECT that counts the rows where the expression changes the value. To keep the data, add a new column with the new type, copy the values, switch the code, and drop the old column in a later release. If cutting the values is intended, suppress this finding with that reason.

message: Changing the type of "orders"."ref" to varchar(8) with a USING expression rewrites the whole "orders" table while blocking reads and writes.
why: ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and rewrites the table and its indexes, unless the old and new types store values the same way (such as a longer varchar, or varchar to text).
safeAlternative: Expand and contract: add a column with the new type, backfill it in batches, switch the code to it, and drop the old column in a later release.
